Day Zero unavoidable in Cape Town?

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
The reality that Cape Town could hit Day Zero on 12 April has finally hit home. Capetonins went into panic mode and stripped the shelves 5 litres of bottled water and plastic containers to collect and store water. Bottled water is being collected around the country and sent to Cape Town to be distributed to old age homes and animal welfare centres. Then it was finally revealed that NONE of the alternative water augmentation would be online by Day Zero whether that April or May, and those that will be online are in very small quantities. The message moved from a well- run city will not run out of water to #Avoiddayzero – it’s entirely down to everyone using 50 litres per person day. It clear Cape Town was on its own and National Water Affairs and Sanitation is leaving them pretty much to their own devices quibbling about the term Day Zero

Summary:
Day Zero plans have become more practical and accessible. JP Smith Councillor for Safety and Security spelt out for the first time how the collection points would function. But the 200 Day Zero water collection points have still not been revealed to the public as they have to ensure that they are on council or provincial land and if they are on private land they still have to get permission to access those site. Now it may be down to 160 sites and the mind boggles how the whole of Cape Town will be serviced by only 160 sites. Traffic congestion in the City is already out of control so the water collection points will have to be on good traffic nodes and they are talking about having drive through sites. Families of 4 can collect 100 litres at a time and water will be free , you will not have to show your ID and the points will remain open till late at night depending on the demand and the area. Informal settlements will not be switched off and very low income areas area will have water but at reduced pressure.
The concern in poor communities is that people are already coming into the informal settlements to collect water from the free standpipes much to the frustration of the residents who have to cue and collect water. When Day Zero hits those surrounding formal houses which are right ontop of the informal areas will just collect water from free standpipes as they will be more accessible than Day Zero collection points.

Press Release:


Day Zero
The fear of the whole of Cape Town queuing for water galvanised residents into action - they brought down their water consumption to just over 500 million litres a day and pushed back Day Zero yet again through their concerted efforts. Some have developed innovative ways to use their swimming pools as reservoirs, while others are spreading their water saving solutions online. Pioneering water treatment is on the cards combining desalination and waste water, and boreholes are being sunk, but have all their efforts been enough to prevent the taps from running dry?


Script:


Script: Day Zero - fact or fake? When Capetonians first heard this apocalyptic term most dismissed it, but when there were a mere 90 days before the taps ran dry, and the whole of Cape Town would be queuing for water – it made international headlines
Marlene “I am frightened … …I mean it’s going to be long cues
Script: Now it’s pulled back to July the 9th, but its sparked panic buying of bottled water- plastic containers and hand sanitizer became scare commodities. Then, water donations started arriving from across the country.
Tania” It amazing how people stand together at a time like this
Script: Thania Wilson-Harris enlisted the Plumstead neighbourhood watch in Cape Town delivering, old age homes and schools
Thania “The more water we can get donated the more chances of day Zero not even arriving
Script: So far 700 tons of water has been delivered. Principal of Westlake Primary Landie Diamond says they are doing everything they can to stave off Day Zero.
Landie “We have switched off and we use sanitizers in our bathrooms. We are currently in the process of repairing our borehole system so that water will be used for sanitation
Link: It is here in the disaster risks management war room that the fine details of Day Zero are thrashed out and the logistics are quite intimidating planning for the equivalent of 10 soccer world cups daily
JP “We have to get 100 more times people into and out of a venue ….everyday and you have to do this continuously until your day zero ends so logistically it will be a huge endeavour …even if it runs perfectly ….it’s still going to be very inconvenient and very unpleasant
Script: JP Smith Mayoral committee member for Safety and Security, says he hopes they will never need them, because they will cost the City anything, between 200 and 400 million rand
JP “ Day Zero again now being deferred first it was the agricultural sector coming off line which pushed it out then we saw a significant reduction in saving. We started well over 800 million litres a day almost a billion litres every day we are now down to just over 500 million litres a day that is a substantial amount in consumption
Script: The Groenland farmers donated their excess water, giving Cape Town another 20 days reprieve.
JP “You can’t say definitively that you are going to have rain in June and July and you can’t say how much you are going to have we could have another disastrous year like last year
Derek “How much notice could you give Capetonians
JP “At least 5 weeks because it will take us at least 5 weeks to build the pods and it takes you 2 weeks to shut down your water reticulation
Script: The City is cutting back everywhere they can.
JP “We are doing certain things like reducing the overall water pressure which saves us 50 million litres a day installing 3500 water demand management devices at the homes of the worst or highest water uses
Link: The informal settlements around the Cape are really vast and as you can see the shacks are densely packed together but surprisingly these residents only use a small fraction of the city’s water supply.
Script: The nearly 500 water points in informal settlements won’t be shut off if Day Zero arrives as they are in effect already water collection points. But Musa Gwebani, from the Social Justice Coalition, is concerned they could become sites of conflict.
Musa “People don’t know how much water they are going to have how much water they are going to lose I was speaking to a lady earlier who says she has about 100 litres of water reserved …because she is selling meat. People that live in informal settlements use 4% of the water in the City ….. people are literally living on the bare minimum of water as it is, so our interventions really are around checking the status of the taps ..are the taps working and trying to detect potential leaks ..and reporting those to the City of Cape Town
Script: The Cities major target is people in formal housing as they consume 55% of the water. Finally it’s dawned on Cape Town that they are the only ones who can save themselves from cuing, and it’s given rise to a slew of water saving tips on social media.
Script: The wealthier have sunk boreholes but they can’t drink, cook or wash with it because of the minerals and contaminants. But, you can drink treated rainwater, and so Mechanical Engineer Andy Cunninghame designed an ingenious system using his pool as a reservoir. His family can survive for 100 days without rain.
Andy “I take the pool cover off for a day when the sun is shining and that evaporates the chlorine and then I take that water which is now bacteria free …through a very fine filter and then an activated carbon filter and store it in a tank.
Script: Andy like most Capetonians, uses the grey water to flush toilets.
Andy “An economical loo takes 7 litres to flush and you will get 5 litres for drinking and cooking so you won’t have anything over for flushing so that’s why … its important to have your own water supply so you can then be independent of the municipality to a very large extent.
Script: Blocked sewers and methane explosions have become a hot topic - but the City has a plan.
JP “By swapping out the drain covers the one is aerated and the one is not to allow the gas to leak out and evaporate… Flushing with ground water or sea water …to keep the system going and we might have to resort to the royal flush the synchronised flushing at a particular time of the day
Script: After a year of telling us
De Lille “A well run City will not run out of water
Script: The message changed to #Defeat day Zero- the truth was out- the water augmentation schemes would not be online in time to save Cape Town
Link” Day Zero is actually when the dams drop down to a mere 13 % and that date is very difficult to predict.
Script “Groundwater is the major alternative water source and they hope to extract 150 million litres a day in total across the peninsular, but it’s not happening anytime soon
John Holmes “The reality is that the augmentation program can have no impact on day Zero
Script: John Holmes of Umvoto Water which co-ordinates the groundwater extraction says the message was wrong from the start
John “We were trying to fast track a process that would have taken several years and said well because there is a crisis now we have to do it in 6 months
Script: This borehole on the Cape Flats is pushing out 50 million litres a day, but not all sites are this pristine – this water smells more like sewerage. The first ground water will start coming into the system only by the end of May. But is this sustainable?
John “I think there are 3 anxieties one is salt water intrusion one is over extracting the aquifer and how sustainable is what we are doing. The 3 are linked…There is a water use process that is very specific about what we can and what we can’t do. Managed aquifer recharge is a condition of those licences.
Script: The bigger concern is the 30 000 boreholes sunk by private users aren’t strictly monitored. A 1000 square meter property is supposed to only use 100 litres a day- but do they?
John “I think this drought is an opportunity to revisit how we monitor this. The days of watering your lawn with borehole water is past. That is a resource that we must all share that needs to last forever
Link: Desalination as a way to solve Cape Town’s water crisis has been much debated over the past year with many miracle promises being made from saviour ships sailing in, to desalination companies saying they could provide the entire Cities requirements at a fraction of the cost.
Script: Desalination is the most expensive water source as it consumes huge amounts of electricity, that’s why this latest and largest tender awarded to Nu Water is a step forward. The plant will deliver 80 mega litres a day ramping up to 100 and what’s set it apart is that it combines desalination and waste water reclamation.
Derek ‘Are you saying you could supply one 5th or more of the cities requirements for water supply in that factory we have just walked through
NJ “Yes that is correct. Currently the Cape Flats pushes out 150 to 170 mega litres per day out to sea with high organic loads and we reclaim that water for production and pump it back into the reticulation grid mixed with water produced from sea water desalination facility
Script Currently there are 3 convention desalination plants being built- the 2 million litres a day at the Water Front, and Monwabisi and Strandfontein each generating 7 million litres daily, but they will only be fully on line by June. The Nu Water project will be ready in 22 weeks, using 50% less electricity, and the water will cost less than half the price of regular desalination.
NJ “The projected cost to produce 100 mega litres a day over a 5 year period is between R15 and R17 per cubic meter
Script: The term Day Zero may have been much debated, but it’s been an essential tool in galvanising people into action.
JP and out of this will have come a series of benefits which is individual houses will have learnt to save water our water augmentation schemes will be there funded by the city, no thanks to National Government and as a City we will have prepared for a Disaster even although it hasn’t come will leave us better prepared for the next one
